findings.highlight: some boundaries I crossed in our conversation that I shouldn't have
findings.evidenceJa: もっと踏み込んだ話題があったはずだけど
findings.explanation: Half-awake, Haruki senses that there had been a deeper, more intimate subject in his conversation with Kazusa. Todokanai TL invents both a boundary violation and his judgment that he should not have crossed it, moralizing a simple failure to recall what they discussed.
findings.japanese:
もっと踏み込んだ話題があったはずだけど、
起き抜けの思考が追いついていかない。
findings.todokanai: I feel like there were some boundaries I crossed in our conversation that I shouldn't have, but having just woken up, I can't remember what it was for the life of me.

findings.highlight: Not having to ask the reason why, I gently put the coat over her shoulders.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺はなんとか理由を聞くことなく、
その肩に、ゆっくりコートをかけていく。
findings.explanation: Haruki somehow manages not to ask why Setsuna has turned her unguarded back to him; “not having to ask” removes his active restraint.
findings.japanese:
俺はなんとか理由を聞くことなく、
その肩に、ゆっくりコートをかけていく。
findings.todokanai: Not having to ask the reason why, I gently put the coat over her shoulders.

findings.evidenceJa: 一線を越えちゃったら二度とやめられなくなりそう
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that once she crosses the line into performing, she feels as though she may never be able to quit. The English turns her potentially addictive exhilaration into the external claim that nothing can stop her.
findings.japanese:
「人前で歌うのって、ものすごく緊張するけど、
一線を越えちゃったら二度とやめられなくなりそう」
findings.todokanai: "The thought of having to sing in front of other people is really scary, but once you cross that line, nothing can really stop you."

findings.highlight: I didn't even wave to them!
findings.evidenceJa: 振りつけとか全然やらなかったね
findings.explanation: Setsuna realizes they did no choreography or dance movements at all. The English substitutes a single missed wave to the audience, changing a reflection on their whole stage presentation into a trivial greeting gesture.
findings.japanese: 「…そういえば振りつけとか全然やらなかったね」
findings.todokanai: "…Come to think of it, I didn't even wave to them!"

findings.highlight: I can see Touma just refusing the idea flat out
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬にはけんもほろろに断られたけどな
findings.explanation: Haruki notes that Kazusa has already rejected his suggestion out of hand. Todokanai TL turns the completed exchange into his prediction of how she would respond, obscuring that he has already asked her about performing again.
findings.japanese: 冬馬にはけんもほろろに断られたけどな…
findings.todokanai: I can see Touma just refusing the idea flat out, though…

findings.evidenceJa: 今のところ政経のつもりだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki says he currently intends to enter political science and economics, the 政経 course or faculty. “Public policy” is a different academic field and breaks the department comparison Setsuna immediately begins.
findings.japanese: 「え？　いや、今のところ政経のつもりだけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Eh? No, right now I'm thinking along the lines of public policy…"

findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether Haruki will join the English Literature department, so they can align their university paths. “Take English” sounds like choosing a class and does not name the degree program under discussion.

findings.highlight: I know that for a fact
findings.explanation: Haruki says he is bad at English only relatively; Setsuna replies that she is bad at politics and economics absolutely. “I know that for a fact” removes the explicit relative/absolute pair on which their teasing exchange is built.
findings.japanese: 「わたしだって政治も経済も苦手だよ。絶対的に」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I'm bad at politics and economics too. I know that for a fact."

findings.highlight: I just couldn't get over my crush
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の心を掴みきれてなかったわたしが悪い
findings.explanation: Setsuna blames herself for failing to grasp her own heart completely and therefore failing to anticipate that she would approach Haruki instead of remaining passive. Todokanai TL says she could not get over a crush she already understood, reversing the line's crucial distinction between self-discovery and failed suppression.
findings.japanese:
「仕方がないか…
自分の心を掴みきれてなかった
わたしが悪いんだもんね」
findings.todokanai: "But I guess I can't help myself… I just couldn't get over my crush, so it's all my own fault, right?"

findings.highlight: has no real reason to resist
findings.evidenceJa: 抵抗なんかするわけがなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki narrates that there was no possibility Setsuna would resist the kiss she had invited. The English instead invents his rationale that she has no reason to resist, changing observed certainty about her response into his judgment about what she is entitled or expected to do.
findings.japanese: 雪菜は…抵抗なんかするわけがなかった。
findings.todokanai: And Setsuna… has no real reason to resist.

findings.highlight: And then, I force myself onto Setsuna once more
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の方が雪菜に押しつけていた
findings.explanation: After Setsuna finally pulls her lips away when Haruki's arms loosen, he realizes retrospectively that he had been the one pressing the kiss onto her. Todokanai TL invents a new second advance after the separation—“once more”—materially changing the physical sequence and sexual agency.
findings.japanese: …俺の方が雪菜に押しつけていた。
findings.todokanai: …And then, I force myself onto Setsuna once more.

findings.highlight: While I, on the other hand… I feel as if I could die in peace over the unimaginably pleasant sensation.
findings.evidenceJa:
そして俺の方は…
あまりにも想像を絶する快感に、
果ててしまいそうになっていた。
findings.explanation: 果ててしまいそう carries a sexual and bodily sense of reaching an endpoint or climax; “die in peace” turns it into a comic death idiom.
findings.japanese:
そして俺の方は…
あまりにも想像を絶する快感に、
果ててしまいそうになっていた。
findings.todokanai: While I, on the other hand… I feel as if I could die in peace over the unimaginably pleasant sensation.
